findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of the authenticated principal for write operations. The upsertProduct and deleteProduct mutations do not log who performed the action. No CloudTrail configuration in the SAM template. No application-level audit event emission.
findings.gap: Write operations execute without recording the authenticated identity. If an agent modifies or deletes catalog data, there is no immutable record of which principal took the action.
findings.recommendation: Add an Apollo Server plugin that logs the authenticated principal (from JWT claims), operation name, and mutation variables to a structured CloudWatch log group with 365-day retention. Enable API Gateway access logging.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no audit logging for write operations
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 fired as BLOCKER because the system exposes write mutations (upsertProduct, deleteProduct) that agents will invoke, yet no audit trail records which principal performed each write.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add Apollo Server plugin for audit logging of write operations with principal identity
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every write operation produces an immutable audit record with principal identity, operation, target SKU, and timestamp

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: JWT claims are extracted from the API Gateway Cognito authorizer and passed to resolvers as scopes. However, there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own service identity vs. acting on behalf of a specific human user.
findings.gap: No explicit distinction between agent-as-self and agent-on-behalf-of-user. All authenticated callers are treated identically based on JWT scopes.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 token exchange or add a custom claim (act claim per RFC 8693) to distinguish delegated calls. Log both the agent identity and the delegating user identity.

compensating_controls: Use distinct Cognito app clients for agent identities with narrower scopes
Include custom X-On-Behalf-Of claim in agent-issued tokens

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: DynamoDB writes in upsertProduct use unconditional put (last-write-wins) with no version field, conditional expression, or ETag. deleteProduct uses unconditional update. Multiple concurrent agent instances could overwrite each other's changes silently.
findings.gap: No optimistic locking or concurrency controls on write operations.
findings.recommendation: Add a version field and use DynamoDB ConditionExpression to implement optimistic locking. Return the version in GraphQL responses.

compensating_controls: Serialize agent write operations through a queue for critical SKUs
Limit concurrent agent instances to one

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: No explicit circuit breaker pattern implemented. The service depends on DynamoDB for all operations. AWS SDK v3 provides default retry with exponential backoff, and Lambda enforces a 30-second timeout, but no circuit breaker prevents cascading failures if DynamoDB experiences sustained degradation.
findings.gap: No fail-fast mechanism for sustained DynamoDB degradation. Sustained throttling would cause all Lambda invocations to consume their full timeout.
findings.recommendation: Implement a lightweight circuit breaker (e.g., opossum library) around DynamoDB calls that opens after N consecutive failures.

compensating_controls: Lambda 30s timeout provides hard ceiling on request duration
AWS SDK default retry with exponential backoff handles transient errors

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No explicit rate limiting configuration in the SAM template. The API Gateway HTTP API uses AWS account-level default throttling but no per-API, per-route, or per-caller throttle is configured.
findings.gap: No explicit rate limits to prevent a runaway agent loop from overwhelming the service.
findings.recommendation: Add ThrottlingBurstLimit and ThrottlingRateLimit to the HttpApi resource. Consider WAF rate rules for per-client throttling.

compensating_controls: API Gateway account-level default throttle (10,000 rps burst)
DynamoDB on-demand auto-scales

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-level transaction limits exist. An agent with catalog:write scope could call upsertProduct or deleteProduct in a loop without any cap on records modified per session or time window.
findings.gap: No configurable limits on records modified per agent identity per time window.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller write quotas (e.g., max 100 upserts/hour per client_id) enforced at the resolver layer.

compensating_controls: Soft-delete design means deletions are recoverable
DynamoDB Point-in-Time Recovery enables full table restoration

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: All write operations are immediately committed. upsertProduct immediately persists the product, and deleteProduct immediately soft-deletes. There is no draft, pending, or proposed state for human review.
findings.gap: No mechanism for an agent to propose changes that a human can review before they take effect.
findings.recommendation: Add a status field to products with values like DRAFT/ACTIVE. Agent-initiated writes create products in DRAFT status requiring human promotion.

compensating_controls: Soft-delete is recoverable (not permanent)
Scope-gating ensures only catalog:write holders can mutate

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No configurable approval gates exist. All mutations execute immediately upon receiving a valid authenticated request with the required scope.
findings.gap: Cannot configure specific operations to require human approval before execution.
findings.recommendation: Implement a configurable approval workflow for high-risk operations (e.g., bulk updates, deletes above a threshold).

compensating_controls: Scope-based authorization limits who can invoke mutations
Soft-delete design means no irreversible data loss

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error handling relies on Apollo Server's default error formatting. Authorization errors throw Error('forbidden: requires scope ...') without custom error codes. DynamoDB SDK errors propagate without structured classification.
findings.gap: No custom GraphQL error codes, no retryable indicator. Agents cannot programmatically distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Add a custom Apollo error formatter that maps errors to structured codes (FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, THROTTLED, INTERNAL) with a retryable boolean in extensions.

compensating_controls: GraphQL standard error format provides message and locations
Apollo Server 4 includes extensions.code for built-in errors

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Products have an updatedAt field set to ISO 8601 UTC. However, there is no createdAt field and no response-level freshness signaling (Cache-Control, staleness indicators).
findings.gap: Partial temporal metadata — no creation timestamp, no freshness signaling.
findings.recommendation: Add a createdAt field populated on first insert. Consider freshness headers in GraphQL responses.

compensating_controls: updatedAt provides last-modification time in UTC
DynamoDB strongly consistent reads available

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: A GraphQL schema file exists providing a documented API contract. However, there is no schema versioning strategy, no breaking-change detection tooling, no changelog, and no contract tests.
findings.gap: Schema changes could break agent tool bindings without detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a schema comparison step to CI (e.g., graphql-inspector) that detects breaking changes. Maintain a schema changelog.

compensating_controls: GraphQL supports additive changes without breaking clients
Schema-first approach means schema file is source of truth

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: X-Ray tracing is active (Tracing: Active in SAM Globals). However, no structured JSON logging library is installed or configured. No explicit logging statements, request correlation IDs, or structured log output in the codebase.
findings.gap: Tracing present but structured logging with correlation IDs is absent.
findings.recommendation: Add @aws-lambda-powertools/logger for structured JSON logs with trace ID and request ID. Add an Apollo Server plugin for request-level logging.

compensating_controls: X-Ray traces provide request-level visibility
Lambda automatically logs invocation start/end with request ID

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms or alerting configuration defined in the SAM template. No anomaly detection, no integration with alerting services.
findings.gap: No alerting to detect when the API is degraded for agents.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for Lambda error rate > 5%, p99 latency > 5s, and DynamoDB throttled requests > 0.

compensating_controls: CloudWatch automatically collects Lambda metrics
X-Ray provides service map for manual investigation

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: Infrastructure is defined as code (SAM template.yaml) defining API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. However, no peer review enforcement and no drift detection are present.
findings.gap: IaC exists (1/3 governance sub-checks) but no automated review enforcement or drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI/CD pipeline with required PR reviews for IaC changes. Enable AWS Config rules for drift detection.

compensating_controls: SAM template provides reproducible deployments
CloudFormation detects drift on demand

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline configuration files found in the repository. package.json defines build, test, and lint scripts for local development only.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline to catch API-breaking changes before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI/CD pipeline that runs lint, test, build, and schema comparison on every PR.

compensating_controls: Local test/build/lint scripts exist
GraphQL schema-first approach makes changes explicit

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No explicit rollback configuration. No blue/green deployment, no canary, no CodeDeploy. CloudFormation provides implicit rollback only on stack update failure.
findings.gap: No fast rollback mechanism for successful-but-broken deployments.
findings.recommendation: Enable Lambda DeploymentPreference with canary/linear and automatic rollback on CloudWatch alarm trigger.

compensating_controls: CloudFormation auto-rollback on update failure
Lambda versioning could be enabled

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: vitest is configured as a dev dependency with a test script, but no test files exist in the repository. Zero automated test coverage.
findings.gap: No tests for the APIs agents will consume.
findings.recommendation: Add resolver unit tests covering successful queries, pagination, scope enforcement, error responses, and idempotent upsert.

compensating_controls: GraphQL schema validation provides type safety
TypeScript provides static type checking

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration in the repository. No docker-compose for local testing, no seed data scripts, no environment-specific configurations.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Add samconfig.toml with staging/production environments. Add docker-compose with DynamoDB Local for local agent testing.

compensating_controls: SAM template can be deployed to multiple environments
DynamoDB Local available for local testing

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: No event emission for state changes. Product upserts and soft-deletes do not publish events to SNS, EventBridge, SQS, or any event bus.
findings.gap: No reactive event surface for downstream consumers or agents.
findings.recommendation: Add EventBridge integration to emit events on product create/update/delete.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limit documentation or headers. The API does not return X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After, or similar headers.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on remaining capacity.
findings.recommendation: Document rate limits in schema description. Configure API Gateway to return throttling headers.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Product catalog data (SKU, name, description, price, currency, active status) contains no PII, PHI, financial records, or credentials. Not a data-handling target for sensitive data.
findings.gap: None — no sensitive data present in this system.
findings.recommendation: Monitor schema evolution — re-evaluate if user-specific or regulated data is added.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Stage A = No: system does not store/process/transmit sensitive data
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 Stage A evaluated as No because the product catalog (sku, name, description, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt) contains no PII, PHI, financial instruments, or credentials.

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality metrics, completeness monitoring, or profiling for the product catalog.
findings.gap: No completeness or quality tracking.
findings.recommendation: Add custom metrics for catalog data quality (completeness, anomalies).

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No dedicated data catalog or metadata layer. The GraphQL schema provides structural documentation but not semantic data lineage or business glossary.
findings.gap: No business glossary or data lineage documentation.
findings.recommendation: Add descriptions to all GraphQL schema fields documenting business meaning.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No custom business outcome metrics published. Only infrastructure-level metrics via Lambda defaults and X-Ray.
findings.gap: No agent-outcome measurement capability.
findings.recommendation: Add custom CloudWatch metrics for catalog operations (products_upserted, products_deleted, queries_per_minute).

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema-first interface with documented queries and mutations via schema/catalog.graphql

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema file serves as machine-readable spec; Apollo Server supports introspection

evaluations.title: Idempotent Write Operations
evaluations.reason: Both mutations are idempotent: upsertProduct uses PutItem by SKU, deleteProduct is a repeatable soft-delete

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: GraphQL returns structured JSON responses via Apollo Server

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operations >30s or long-running workflows detected

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: Cognito JWT authorizer configured with support for app client credentials (machine identity) and principal attribution via JWT sub claim

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: JWT scopes differentiate access (catalog:write for mutations, any auth for reads); IAM scoped to specific table

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Mutations require catalog:write scope; reads require only authentication — action-level differentiation exists

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: No hardcoded credentials; DynamoDB via IAM role; Cognito UserPoolId as CFN parameter

evaluations.title: Agent Identity Suspension
evaluations.reason: Cognito supports disabling individual users/app clients; JWT authorizer rejects tokens from disabled identities

evaluations.title: Compensation and Rollback
evaluations.reason: Operations are single-step atomic DynamoDB calls with no multi-step workflows. Soft-delete is reversible. PITR enabled.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: Current state fully queryable via product(sku) and products(limit, cursor) queries

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority specified and critical path not determined

evaluations.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
evaluations.reason: Product catalog data (SKU, name, price) is not subject to residency restrictions — not PII, PHI, or regulated financial data

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Pagination with configurable limit (default 50), cursor-based navigation, and GraphQL field selection

evaluations.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
evaluations.reason: GraphQL schema enforces non-null types and input shapes; Apollo Server returns structured validation errors

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: System handles product catalog data (no PII). No user-identifiable information in data model.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are human-readable and semantic: sku, name, description, priceCents, currency, active, updatedAt

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB SSESpecification SSEEnabled: true — server-side encryption enabled

items.summary: Resolve the audit logging blocker and address critical safety controls: concurrency, circuit breakers, rate limiting, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Address remaining safety risks (identity delegation, blast radius) and establish quality foundation (CI/CD, observability, schema versioning).
Add test coverage, event emission for reactive agents, rate limit headers, and business metrics.
Address informational findings: data classification monitoring, quality metrics, and data catalog documentation.

recommended_actions.action: Implement audit logging for all write operations
recommended_actions.rationale: Only BLOCKER finding. Add Apollo Server plugin to log principal identity, operation, and target on every mutation. Unblocks agent deployment.

recommended_actions.action: Add rate limiting and concurrency controls
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents data corruption from concurrent writes and protects against runaway agent loops. Required for safe write-enabled agent operation.

recommended_actions.action: Establish CI/CD pipeline with schema validation
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents undetected breaking changes to the GraphQL schema that would silently break agent tool bindings.
Enables debugging of agent-initiated request failures and alerting on service degradation.
